links.outcome: Reading grade level of patient education materials before vs after LLM simplification
links.effect: Average reading level fell from 10.59 ± 2.20 to 8.44 ± 1.84 (ChatGPT-4o), 7.50 ± 2.10 (Gemini 2.0), and 7.01 ± 0.91 (DeepSeek-R1), P < 0.001.
links.quote: After LLM conversion, the readability improved significantly, with the average reading level reduced to 8.44 ± 1.84 using ChatGPT-4o, 7.50 ± 2.10 with Gemini 2.0, and 7.01 ± 0.91 with DeepSeek-R1 ( P < 0.001 ).

links.outcome: Whether prompting LLMs to simplify materials achieves sixth-grade reading level
links.effect: Zero-shot-CoT (APE) prompt achieved Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 5.81 ± 0.44, below the sixth grade target; prompt strategies differed significantly (P<0.01).
links.quote: Among them, Zero-shot-CoT (APE) showed the most notable improvement, achieving a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level score of 5.81 ± 0.44 and a Flesch Reading Ease score of 72.27 ± 2.59, successfully reducing the reading level below the sixth grade target.

links.outcome: Reading level of PEMs generated directly by LLMs and existing online PEMs
links.effect: LLM-generated PEMs averaged 13.85 ± 1.89 grade level; Google PEMs averaged 10.59 ± 2.20, far above the recommended sixth grade level.
links.quote: The average reading grade level was 13.85 ± 1.89.

links.outcome: Reading level of existing online PEMs versus recommended sixth grade
links.effect: Google-sourced PEMs averaged 10.59 ± 2.20 grade level; first 10 results better but all far exceeded sixth grade.
links.quote: Notably, the first 10 search results had better readability than the subsequent 40 results, although all far exceeded the recommended sixth grade level.

links.outcome: Readability output variation across different prompt phrasings for same source materials
links.effect: Different prompt engineering strategies had significant impact on readability (FKGL P<0.01, Gunning Fog P<0.01, SMOG P<0.01, Coleman-Liau P=0.03; Flesch Reading Ease P=0.09).
links.quote: Readability calculations based on five standard formulas indicate that different prompt engineering strategies had a statistically significant impact on the readability of the final converted PEMs.
